title: Investigation of Lamotrigine Crystal Polymorphs Using Crystal Structure Prediction and Terahertz Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Crystal structure prediction (CSP) plays a significant role in exploring the crystal polymorphism of pharmaceutical solids. Determination of the atomic-level structures of crystalline materials is a fundamental step in understanding their bulk physical and chemical properties and behavior in drug products. CSP can be performed using numerous computational approaches, but all ultimately require comparison with experimental measurements to confirm the CSP findings. In this work, terahertz (THz) vibrational spectroscopy is combined with powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to demonstrate a new metrics framework for the validation of CSP investigations. Terahertz spectroscopy probes the low-frequency (≤150 cm−1) lattice vibrations of molecular crystals and provides a polymorph specific spectral profile that complements diffraction methods. This methodology is applied to the anti-epileptic drug lamotrigine, the subject of multiple crystal engineering studies to improve its formulated performance. summary: Combines terahertz spectroscopy with PXRD as a joint validation metric for CSP-generated lamotrigine polymorph candidates, beyond diffraction-only confirmation.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Crystal Structural Prototypes: Construction, Classification, and Applications
abstract: Crystal structural prototypes describe recurring atomic arrangements across chemically distinct materials. Prototype libraries are built through crystallographic curation, standardization, geometric matching, local-environment clustering, and periodic-graph analysis, and support chemical substitution, derivative enumeration, high-throughput screening, structure solution, crystal structure prediction (CSP), and generative design. This survey compares methods by the structural information they retain and the equivalence rules they impose, distinguishing crystallographic structure types, geometric realizations, chemistry-anonymous topologies, and chemical decorations. We review curated and automatically extracted prototype libraries (AFLOW, CSPD, LAE-ICSPD, EMFDTW, TYPIX, ICSD structure types), their source databases, and algorithms for assigning family membership. A GraphID-based analysis of samples from ICSD, the Materials Project, OQMD, and LeMat shows that the 100 most frequent families in each sample cover 30 to 67 percent of analyzed structures, while 72 to 82 percent of observed families are singletons. The GraphIDs of up to 76 percent of structures change when the neighbor tol

summary: Provides a comparative survey and GraphID-based empirical analysis of crystal prototype libraries, quantifying family frequency/singleton distributions and neighbor-tolerance sensitivity across ICSD, Materials Project, OQMD, and LeMat.

title: A MACE interatomic potential for two dimensional and curved sp2 carbon: family level transfer benchmarks and a SOAP based structural novelty map

screen.reason: MLIP (MACE) development with transfer-learning benchmarks; direct tool for CSP acceleration.

summary: A single MACE interatomic potential is trained across multiple sp2 carbon families (planar and curved) and benchmarked for cross-family transferability using a SOAP-based descriptor map that quantifies structural novelty relative to the training set.

title: CrystalAR: Autoregressive Modeling for Symmetric Crystal Generation
abstract: Deep generative modeling has achieved remarkable progress in crystal generation. Given the rich symmetries inherent in crystalline structures, recent work has sought to explicitly incorporate space-group symmetry into generative models, enabling more effective exploration of novel symmetry templates. Yet introducing symmetry templates increases the combinatorial complexity of stoichiometric relationships between atomic species and crystallographic sites, while creating a fundamental tension between flexible exploration of discrete crystallographic templates and faithful realization of these templates as continuous three-dimensional structures. To address these challenges, we propose CrystalAR, a unified autoregressive framework that models Wyckoff symmetry templates and complete crystal structures within a single generative sequence. Specifically, CrystalAR reformulates continuous coordinate generation as a symmetry-conditioned hierarchy of discrete spatial localization decisions, autoregressively refining the positions of all symmetry-inequivalent sites across resolution levels while jointly modeling their spatial configuration within each level. screen.reason: Autoregressive generative model with explicit symmetry handling; direct polymorph candidate generation method with trans

summary: Introduces CrystalAR, a single autoregressive model that jointly generates Wyckoff symmetry templates and continuous atomic coordinates via hierarchical discretized spatial localization, unifying symmetry-template exploration with structure realization.

title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
abstract: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and c

screen.reason: Active learning for MLIPs directly accelerates CSP workflows; uncertainty-driven sampling optimizes training data for st

summary: Synthesizes 70+ studies into a unified taxonomy of uncertainty-driven active-learning strategies for interatomic potentials, tracing their evolution from on-the-fly MD toward data-efficient fine-tuning of pretrained models.

title: All-electron machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems
abstract: We introduce STRUCTURES-P, a machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems. Electrostatics are evaluated analytically in an atom-centered Gaussian basis, while an equivariant network learns the kinetic and exchange-correlation energy from energies and gradients of non-ground-state densities. Minimizing the functional from a superposition of atomic densities recovers the Kohn-Sham ground state: on held-out crystals, the density error falls from 6.7% to 0.4% of the electron count and the energy error reaches 0.25 mHa per atom, half that of a same-architecture interatomic potential. A single functional can be trained for both isolated molecules and periodic systems, and the model generalizes to larger unit cells. It largely preserves relative-energy rankings and reproduces convex-hull vertices on the tested H-N composition slice. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of machine-learned all-electron orbital-free DFT for variational density optimization and energy evaluation in fixed-geometry solids.

screen.reason: ML orbital-free DFT for CHNO crystals; rapid energy evaluation for CSP ranking, but limited to fixed geometries.

summary: Introduces STRUCTURES-P, an equivariant machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional trained on non-ground-state densities, enabling variational density optimization that recovers Kohn-Sham energetics for periodic CHNO crystals and molecules alike.

title: Accuracy of Vibrational Properties of Machine-Learning Force Fields for Molecular Crystal Transformations
abstract: Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) enable the calculation of transformation pathways in molecular crystals at a fraction of the computational cost of density functional theory (DFT). However, a good agreement in energies and structures does not necessarily imply an accurate description of vibrational properties, which are essential for characterizing transition states and determining free energies at finite temperatures. Herein, we assess the accuracy of system-specific SO3krates MLFFs trained on PBE+MBD reference data for describing vibrational properties of molecular crystal transformations. As examples, we consider a polymorph transition of 1,4-diiodobenzene and a single-crystal-to-single-crystal Diels-Alder reaction. The transition state structures obtained from solid-state nudged-elastic-band (NEB) calculations with the MLFFs exhibit a single imaginary $Γ$-point frequency associated with the respective transformation. Compared with PBE+MBD, the mean absolute errors of $Γ$-point vibrational frequencies and relative harmonic free energies at 300 K are about 3 cm$^{-1}$ and 1 kJ/mol, respectively. Furthermore, we compare for the Diels-Alder reaction a collective transformation

screen.reason: MLFF accuracy for molecular crystal transformations; direct polymorph-transition methodology with vibrational validation

summary: Systematically benchmarks SO3krates MLFFs against PBE+MBD for Γ-point vibrational frequencies and harmonic free energies at transition states of molecular crystal transformations, revealing sub-kJ/mol accuracy previously unverified.

title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, w

summary: Introduces an unsupervised, single-run training method that tracks per-sample loss via exponential moving average to automatically down-weight noisy reference data without extra DFT calculations or retraining cycles.

title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives

screen.reason: Novel MLIP training paradigm; avoids derivative computation for potential fitting.

summary: A Hessian-informed interatomic potential trained to predict energies and forces directly without requiring explicit derivative (force/Hessian) computations, likely speeding up relaxation and transition-state searches in CSP workflows.

title: Linear response for machine-learned interatomic potentials: phonons at arbitrary wave vectors from the primitive cell
abstract: Phonon calculations with machine-learned interatomic potentials are almost exclusively performed with finite displacements in supercells, an approach that is exact only at wave vectors commensurate with the supercell and whose error depends on the range of the force constants. In message-passing networks this range grows with the number of layers, and reaches 140 angstrom for the deepest universal models. Here we show that the dynamical matrix of a message-passing potential can be obtained exactly in the primitive cell, at any wave vector, as the linear response of the forces to a displacement modulated by a Bloch phase, in the spirit of density-functional perturbation theory. The phase enters only where the features of neighboring atoms are gathered, and the trained model is used without modification. One further derivative yields group velocities and mode Grüneisen parameters analytically. We apply the method to NequIP and Prophet, and reproduce the Hessians of supercells to machine precision. screen.reason: MLIP phonon methodology; transfer to lattice-energy ranking via Hessian; modest direct CSP relevance.

summary: Introduces a density-functional-perturbation-theory-style linear-response method enabling exact, arbitrary-wavevector phonon dynamical matrices directly from message-passing potentials' primitive cells, bypassing supercell finite-displacement errors.

title: Unconstrained learning of equivariant atomistic properties
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have made first-principles accuracy routine for the potential energy surface (PES). Their backbones, often O(3)-equivariant by design, are increasingly used to learn other atomistic properties. Many of these are of high angular order or pseudotensorial character, defined per atom, or expanded on large atom-centered basis sets. Such targets strain equivariant GNNs, whose tensor products grow steeply in cost with angular order and can fail to represent the target if truncated, forcing difficult trade-offs between hyperparameters. Unconstrained models like the Point-Edge Transformer (PET) instead replace explicit O(3) algebra with edge-to-edge attention and learn equivariance from data, so that the same backbone can in principle learn any equivariant property. We demonstrate how to use PET to learn molecular dipoles and polarizabilities, NMR chemical shielding tensors, and auxiliary-basis expansions of the electron density. Increasing the backbone size systematically improves both accuracy and equivariance error, and targeted architectural and training choices reduce the symmetry breaking further. PET matches

title: Foundation-Model Supervision of Distilled Potentials for Million-Atom Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials distilled from foundation models enable fast large-scale molecular dynamics (MD), but they can fail locally in chemical environments that their training data did not sample. System-averaged error metrics and small random audits often miss such sparse or isolated failures. Here we use an exact equivariant foundation model, MACE-MPA-0, to check every atom of million-atom production simulations. Reorganizing two-layer MACE inference into a receiver-chunked three-pass schedule that keeps no per-edge intermediates resident reduces the marginal memory per atom 340-fold, evaluates up to $2.86\times10^{7}$ atoms on a single H200 GPU, and supervises $10^{6}$-atom trajectories in LAMMPS at 1.3% of the run time. Distilled MACE students run four to nine times slower than NEP89 with 0.95-1.28 times the teacher's force error against density functional theory (DFT). In molten SiO$_2$, whole-system checks uncover a persistent tail of under-coordinated atoms hidden by the system-averaged error and an isolated, unphysical O-O contact that a 1% random audit misses 94% of the time. On-the-fly retraining on teacher-labelled 13-Å clusters, with the force loss restr

screen.reason: MLIP distillation and foundation-model supervision directly applicable to CSP lattice-energy ranking; large-scale MD val

summary: Introduces a memory-efficient MACE inference schedule enabling atom-wise, whole-trajectory DFT-level auditing of million-atom MD, exposing rare local failures invisible to averaged metrics or random sampling.

title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
abstract: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. The proliferation of datasets, with properties often computed using different levels of electronic-structure approximation, is problematic, as there is often overlap between different datasets, and strong correlations between structures obtained with short molecular dynamics trajectories or geometry optimization. To address these problems, we introduce a protocol to stratify a dataset into a hierarchy of nested subsets, subsampling from the coarsest to the finest resolution based on an "ecumetric" built to reflect the latent space representation of several popular universal machine-learning interatomic potentials. We then use this approach to combine most of the open structural datasets currently available, consolidating them into MAD-COSMO, a well-organized collection of almost 1.7 billion structures, whose $2^{24}$ most diverse members form

screen.reason: Large-scale ML dataset for universal MLIPs; diversity sampling aids MLIP training for CSP acceleration.

summary: Introduces an "ecumetric"-based hierarchical subsampling protocol to merge overlapping open structural datasets into MAD-COSMO, a deduplicated ~1.7-billion-structure hierarchy with nested diverse subsets.

title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Automated materials discovery requires evaluating large pools of candidate configurations, with density functional theory (DFT) as a major throughput bottleneck. Pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate DFT cheaply, but their errors vary by orders of magnitude across configurations, making it difficult to decide when to trust the MLIP predictions and when to fall back to DFT. We frame this decision as a risk-controlled selection problem and solve it within a conformal risk control (CRC) framework. Each configuration is mapped from atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates to a fixed geometric descriptor, which a lightweight predictor uses to estimate an MLIP-DFT disagreement score in energy, average force, and maximum force. CRC then calibrates this score into a selection threshold for DFT labeling such that the MLIP error on the unselected configurations, which keep their MLIP labels, stays below a user-chosen fraction $α$ of the expected error. Under an identical guarantee across eight dataset-MLIP pairs, our predictor routes 7% and 14% fewer configurations to DFT at $α=0.3$ than committee baselines. Because committee disagreement overlooks errors the

screen.reason: MLIP error quantification & selective DFT labeling directly accelerates CSP screening workflows.

summary: Introduces a conformal-risk-control framework with a lightweight geometric-descriptor predictor of MLIP–DFT disagreement, selectively routing configurations to DFT with guaranteed error bounds, cutting DFT calls 7–14% versus committee methods.

title: LunaTP: Enabling Efficient and Scalable Tensor Product for Equivariant MLIPs
abstract: Equivariant machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise atomistic simulations with accuracy approaching that of quantum-mechanical calculations. However, the high computational cost of their core Clebsch--Gordan tensor product (CGTP) convolutions severely limits model scalability and efficiency. In this paper, we rethink the parallel execution of CGTP convolutions and introduce LunaTP. Built on node-centric execution, LunaTP exploits path-group parallelism and multi-level reuse to accelerate CGTP convolutions and higher-order derivative computation while preserving the underlying mathematical formulation. On an NVIDIA H100 GPU, LunaTP achieves kernel speedups of up to 250.0$\times$ over e3nn and 17.1$\times$ over OpenEquivariance. It also delivers end-to-end training throughput gains of up to 28.7$\times$ over e3nn and 3.11$\times$ over OpenEquivariance. Finally, LunaTP demonstrates scalability and robust performance across models, workload scales, and GPUs, delivering substantial acceleration for training and atomistic simulation with high-accuracy equivariant MLIPs.

screen.reason: MLIP computational efficiency directly enables faster CSP ranking; equivariant architectures core to modern potentials.

summary: LunaTP introduces path-group parallelism and multi-level reuse for node-centric Clebsch–Gordan tensor product execution, achieving up to 250× kernel and 28.7× training speedups over e3nn.
